My friend, everything is ready. I hope that my father and my beloved sister will be the victim he ordered.
If I'm not mistaken, it's Apollo you're paying homage to.
It's him.

So Oebalus prepares such solemn sacrifices for Apollo? Does he not know that there are other gods in heaven? Is it not necessary for Semele's son, for Juno, Venus, Diana, Mars, Volcano, for the mighty head, the prince of the Heavenly, your incense?

We sacrifice to all gods, Zephyr, no one goes out of our temples ungifted; but this temple has reserved Apollo for his glory. The Father worships him as a mighty deity, and according to the example of the Father also I.
I would love to offer my heart to you if you were my apoll!
Dear Zephyr, why do you confuse me with gods? I do not consider myself worthy of worship, but I know that the too great love for Hyacinth has wrestled these words from you.
My father and my sister.
Say, my son, is sacrifice and fire ready?
Behold, my Father, according to your desire, everything is ready and waiting for your arrival.
Rightly so: the offering servant, therefore, put fire on the stove, abundant incense is pouring on the altar, and the smoke of the offering is rising to the clouds.
Oh, my father, with black clouds, an imminent storm rises, the whole sky covers the night.

Here! No longer hesitation tolerates Apollo, he demands of us frankincense and sacrifices. Before your prayers the grey weather will escape and the friendly face of the sun will shine again to this land ... well! And speak with me the prayers.
Goddess from Latona's lap!
Hear the supplication of the supplications,
three times worthy of honor,
who they consecrate to you,
Your goodness, your grace
Follow them forever.
O Apollo, protect
always and worthy

my country Laconia.
Deity from Latonas Schoss! etc.
Woe! We are lost! God rejects our prayers!
Did any of you offend God?
No, Father, I'm not aware of any fault.
I have always worshipped this God.
(Zephyr, I'm afraid the words you spoke earlier have kindled this anger.)
(Hyazinth, if you are my friend, hide from the father, keep away the words we said earlier!)
The fire was extinguished, the altar fell, the sacrifice was despised! Great calamity prophesied to us. Woe! I was shaken by this flash of lightning, I trembled all over my body!

Man thee, Father! Guilty is thy heart; so what canst thou fear of the good deity evil? The lightning hath not hurt thee, none of us, as many as we are, hath fallen. We live, and all rejoice health as before: the God wanted with this lightning to frighten the earth, that his power might be more manifest to the world, and that fear of God, coupled with trust, might be preserved in us.
The gods often startle,
stand up and threaten,

who frightens us,

which do not meet;
but after played weather

so also by terror
they bind to themselves the peoples:
Now to love,

Repose her glory.

Oh, my son, what you say is true, and yet I fear that Apoll could destroy Oebalus by this flame.
Apollo hears, O believe, your petitions, and he promises his help to this land, if you only want to receive him, the exiled, who has learned to hate the wrath of lightning-scattering Jupiter.
How? ... The God, physically present, hiding in this garment of a shepherd, wishes to be admitted into our country?
See, Father! How the Heavenly likes to play with us! Already after the terrible wound the God brings the healing and pleases your king's castle through his presence.

O how fortunate is the star with which this clouded day refreshes us by visiting our house as a desirable guest! ... Oh what grace! What beauty! ... What dignity! ... What splendor and what excellency shines from all its members!
Melia, what do you see about the shepherd worthy of such an astonishment?
I see...
What do you see?
I see the beautiful Apollo, to whom I have long consecrated my heart with my father.
That you are consecrated, the heart, do not take back! Of all the gifts of the earth, this is my most acknowledgment.

Oh, great miracle, if you can be Hyacinth's friend!

Happy day! Holy God! Enter my house, and if you consider it worthy to remain in it, stay with us for a long time, I beg you.

To the God worthy of three times our worship, will you, my child, I doubt, consecrate your love?

Don't doubt Apollo wants you to be his wife, and I - but you decide freely, my daughter - I gladly assured him of my consent at his request.

Can you believe, Father, that I will deny him my Yes? What girl would a God as husband, such a high honor, despise and stand in the way of her happiness if she were not foolish and not powerful in her senses?

You act wisely, my daughter, if you choose this marriage; for then your brother and your father will become, and my grandchildren will be distinguished by a divine lot, and our house by this marriage will become a house of gods.
Tell me, where is Apollo? ... Can I already enjoy his incomparable conversation!
He's practicing with your brother, and with Zephyr, throwing in the grove in the discus, but I hope he'll come back soon and ask your word in my presence.
He will have everything his heart desires.

I'm telling the truth, I was a witness when he was fatally hit. As soon as Hyazinth had fallen, I fled from the fact that no similar calamity hit my head.

So, Deity, do you strike the guiltless? ... The grace with which I have received you deserved to be kissed by the death of my only son? ... Do you, false Deity, also remember to tear Melia away from the Father in this way?
Oh, far be it from me, Father, to choose him as a husband and to hand to the God, who is stained with my brother's blood, to the marriage covenant!
(What do I hear? God thinks of marriage? Does he also want to rob me of the beloved Melia? He, who snatched from me Hyacinth's love, should also rob me of her love?)
Zephyr, what caused the unruly to commit this crime?

I don't know anything. Your son stayed on the lovely shore of the Eurotas, and when he saw that his discus had come closest to the target, he cried out: "My discus, see, is farther than yours and has reached the goal." Apollo hurled his discus and directed him on the boy's head. He fell to the ground. I don't doubt that the force of the discus has fatally injured him.

Does the God have no hesitation in speeding up so that he robs his offspring of Oebalus, who is well disposed for him? So let the deity that is hostile to me be banished from my kingdom. Up, Zephyr! Go on driving the guilty ones away, before he does even more and worse to me!
King, yours is the kingdom; you yourself drive out the wicked; he has offended you by the death of your son; I am afraid of the God who could hurl the lightning on my head.
(I hope that he will drive him away so that my attack may remain hidden; I am the one who committed the murder!)

I go! You stay! When God comes, tell him to go away, my child, the cruel! I go to the Eurotas-Ufer to see my son if he is still alive. Perhaps I will meet Apollo, the God who is so hostile to my kingdom.
(It goes as desired, my plan succeeds, now the beloved Melia remains to me.)
I don't understand why Apollo, insulted by nothing, would have killed the only hyacinth he loved. How could he love me, the sister, if he first defiled his hand with my brother's blood?

Beloved, don't be surprised that Apollo has committed such a crime; you do not know the unruly: he is clever, cruel, impermanent, and light-hearted; therefore he was banished from heaven, that by his wrath he might not disturb the harmony of the gods.
Better to believe of such a great God commands reason.

Melia, what are you rolling in your heart? Ah, cast away the bridegroom, whose hand is clinging to the blood of your brother. Happiness Zephyr, whose faithfulness you know.
Now my brother's fate is on my mind, not a wedding with Zephyr.
Can you despise Zephyr like that?

Protect me, I beg you, before the God! I am innocent!

There you are, murderer! Unheard-of fraud master! Wasn't it enough for you to rob me of my friend Hyacinth? Are you, scoundrel, at the same time also my bride to take away from me and increase your crime, liar, by new crimes? Unruly! Find out immediately what the deity, angry with you, is capable of! Learn the revenge of the loving but also corrupting God, corrupting with justice! You winds, approach! Aeolus, include the criminal in your cave!
What's wrong?
What are you doing, God, in your wrath? Will you depopulate my father's kingdom? The brother is dead, now you also kill Zephyr? Tyrant! Now you will destroy Melia and the king?
O love!
How dare you call me love?
If you don't like listening to me...
It is abhorrent, be silent! Rely on the place of our kingdom! My Father commands it that you do not cause more harm!
(Oh, put out the lightning, Father of the gods! How long will your anger haunt me?)
Escape, you evil man! I am glad,
when the tyrant leaves me!

who breaks the law!
Escape!
For I am afraid of you!

Apollo, full of love for you.
A guilty man,

If you disdain me.
Shall I, helpless against the wrath of heaven,
also play the exile on earth?
I want to stay!

If you love your father, tell me who your killer is!
Zephyr ... Oh! if only ... the God ... was there! ...

O Father! Death ... is bitter!
My son!
Father! ... Ah! Farewell! ...

Hyazinth! ... My son! ... His life is over ... He no longer breathes! ... "Apollo is innocent", he said. "O Father, believe me, he is not! Zephyr is to my death." So you deal with me, Zephyr, you arch-faithful! So you do not hesitate to accuse the God himself of such a great crime and deceive me, your King? Blood-thirsty, with your own blood I will let you bear your crime! ... Should I leave my son's death unforgiven?
Like a ship above the mountains on a raging sea,
is hurled through valleys of waves,
soon it is at the top, near to the clouds;
Soon it swims deep down, close to Tartarus:
so pouring out of the ravenous heart
the gall by my body, my veins, my limbs;
Anger is tearing me up;
Pain pushes me down.
Anger and Vengeance
Shake me constantly.
As on the raging sea, etc.
Wherever I turn, I have seen the horrific deeds of the cruel God in my eyes. First I saw Zephyr's end, now I see my brother, the blameless, lying in his blood.
What are you doing here, my daughter, without company?
I ordered him to leave our kingdom immediately: the ruthless God did not shy away from accumulating murder for new murders.
What do you say, my daughter, what murder are you talking about?
O king, he has taken away the friend, Zephyr, and has let him be torn away from the storms in my sight.

Oh, Apollo is just when he punishes the crime that the treacherous and merciless Zephyr has inflicted on God! He is the author of the murder, daughter, not Apollo: Zephyr has not hesitated to throw the discus at your brother.
But from where, Father, could you find out?
My son told me, because I found him alive, and he's different in my arms.
Woe to me! How, Father? Then why did you order the God to leave your kingdom?
Moved by pain, daughter, and betrayed by Zephyr's trick, I remember. Who would have feared such a ruthless crime of Zephyr?
O Father! Now we are all completely lost! The God, even the God, has forsaken us. Believe me, he will not leave such reproach unpunished.
What, daughter, you think the God has already left us?
I don't doubt it, because I myself have asked Apollo to leave your kingdom, to avoid our house, that I could call him back!
Woe! What an ominous message come upon us today!
The Son dead, the God,
without me wanting to,
without knowing,
offended, leave us.
Without God's Protection
the kingdom will not last long:
O God, I beg, let go
change your mind,
Return to us!
The brother dead,
At your command,
to my pain
The fiancée leaves me.
Bride without groom,
I beg you,
Who should she love?
Do not punish the beloved!
God, oh, return!

King, the love of Hyacinth forces me to return. Forgive me that I, as God, dare to please your kingdom through my presence! Learn what the Deity can do! Hyacinth, rise! Cover your tomb with the flower that is like you and is called after you.
O Almighty God! blushing with shame, I plead guilty. At Zephyr's word, at my Father's command, I have done all that I have done.

Good God, forgive! I have trusted the villain Zephyr, and I have believed that by your guilt my son has found death. O how much evil has the wicked brought upon my kingdom if you do not exercise mercy!
O deity! Do not believe that I have despised you because I called you gone. I was unwise, too gullible, and the anger snatched me from words that the pain of my brother's death gave me.
Be strong, O king! Apollo will not avoid your kingdom. He will abide and remain if you fulfill your promise.
Look, my daughter, who honors God, to choose you as his wife.
Should I believe that he, a god, can love Melia?
O believe! Even Jupiter often loves mortal women; for the cause of the gods is to love yours to be loved.
Deity, look at your maid who, instead of her father, takes her heart to you.

Behold, if a mortal bride please thee, Apollo, receive my daughter out of my hand, and abide forever in my kingdom. Hyacinth is dead; another hyacinth thou shalt be unto me, if thou lett down, than my son-in-law to dwell with us.
Oebalus! I gladly receive from you Melia's hand and will always provide you with kind help.
So your righteousness, God, shines out brighter.
So the innocent does not escape the due reward.
So future generations will praise your mildness.
